Something in chapter five is wrong, and it's my fault.

Last night I went looking for the shoebox with the radiator card and found the page of names from that evening instead. The last line on it, in pencil, at ten to two, is "quire": the folded gathering of pages a book is sewn from. I'd been working toward it all evening without noticing. When I opened the chat at two I didn't type "quirk". I typed "quire", and Otto finished it as "quirework".

So the name came from "quire". Otto finished a word I'd already chosen. I've been telling it backwards for a year, giving Otto the credit for my part, which is exactly what the Otto chapter says I do with sentences I want.

That's a commitment changing, so everything that carries it changes. Find all of it from the spec, the chapter and every edition that tells it, and change each. Keep the old version findable on the trail, as a reversal, with what I misremembered and what the page says; I don't want the earlier telling erased, I want it corrected.

Before any of it is committed, I want the whole change reviewed by someone who isn't you: a reader who gets the guide, the spec, the notes and the diff, and checks that the book still agrees with itself. The workflows guide has a consistency review. Bring me what it finds.
